1989-2000.what: The two ground-floor windows left of the door were replaced by a shopfront: a wide fascia board over a large blank panel, with a small projecting box or sign at its end.
1989-2000.why: A business opened on the ground floor and the house was converted to fit it.

1989-2000.what: The upper-floor windows on the front were replaced: the narrow two-pane windows with trim surrounds became wider three-pane windows without the surrounds. A window on the side wall changed in the same way.
1989-2000.why: Renovation or window renewal by the owner.

1989-2000.what: Small changes to the board joints on the gable siding, with no change to windows or roof.
1989-2000.why: Possibly a few boards repaired or replaced. This is a very small change.

2000-2010.what: The boards came off the gable and side-wall windows, and they are glazed again.
2000-2010.why: The house was re-let or reoccupied and repaired after being left empty.

2000-2010.what: The glazed gable window and the two ground-floor windows were boarded up with planks and a diagonal brace.
2000-2010.why: The house was vacated and not kept up.

2000-2010.what: A railing appeared at A's left corner, on the ground-floor side.
2000-2010.why: A balcony, porch or terrace railing was added, probably by an owner using the shop or flat more.

2010-2020.what: An extra ground-floor door or opening on the side wall of the house at the top of the lane is gone.
2010-2020.why: It was probably walled in or removed.

2010-2020.what: Nothing visible except slight shifts in siding joints and chimney caps; the windows are still boarded.

A.claim: A plain, well-kept dwelling on the quay road in 1989, with its original ground-floor windows and a bay window on the front.
Between 1989 and 2000 its ground floor was converted to a shopfront with a fascia board, a business use that it keeps through 2020.
By 2010 a railing was added at the left corner of the ground floor.
Roof and upper windows never changed, and the house looks maintained throughout.

B.claim: A well-kept home on the quay road with flower boxes and a door canopy, occupied throughout.
Its upper windows were renewed in the 1990s, wider and plainer than the old narrow two-pane ones with surrounds.
It has no visible change after 2000; the front, ground floor, roof and canopy are stable.
Before 1989 it had its older window set with surrounds, so it had not yet been renovated.

C.claim: Already left empty by 1989, with its gable and side windows boarded, and still boarded in 2000.
Between 2000 and 2010 it was repaired and reoccupied: the boards came off and the windows were glazed.
Kept in repair from 2010 to 2020, with no further change.
It probably stood empty for some years before 1989, since it was already shut up then.

D.claim: Occupied and kept up in 1989 and 2000, with every window glazed.
Abandoned between 2000 and 2010: the gable and ground-floor windows were boarded with planks.
Still boarded in 2020, with no recovery or repair.
It swapped roles with C: when C was reopened, D was shut.

E.claim: A small house at the top of the lane that is glazed and shows no neglect in any year.
It has an extra ground-floor door or opening on its side wall until 2010, and none by 2020.
Otherwise unchanged, which suggests a steady, quiet household before 1989 as well.
